correctness.rationale: For every \(j\ge0\), the identities \(f_{2j}=j mod2\) and \(f_{2j+1}=f_j\) forbid alternating length-four factors. Consequently the parity of the start position is recognized by factors of length at least eight. For \(n\ge16\), identical even-start length-\(n\) factors correspond exactly to identical length-\(\lfloor n/2floor\) factors, and odd-start factors to length-\(\lceil n/2ceil\) factors; the alternating phase is fixed by the shorter-factor equality. Monotonicity then gives \(R(n)=2R(\lfloor n/2floor)\). An explicit list certifies twenty-four distinct length-eight factors, and positions eight and twenty-four have identical length-fifteen factors; direct comparison covers the seven shorter base cases. Induction yields \(R(n)=3\cdot2^{\lfloor\log_2nfloor}\) for \(n\ge8\), with unique earlier start \(2^{\lfloor\log_2nfloor}\). The standalone program `verify.py` tests every length through 320 and seventeen selected larger lengths through 8191, with exact integer windows. No infinite claim rests on finite tests alone.

value.rationale: The initial non-repetitive complexity of a classical automatic word is determined exactly at every positive length, including its earlier collision partner. The parity-recognition/decimation proof reveals a sharp binary staircase and ratios to factor length and the known \(p_f(n)=4n\) with distinct lower and upper limits. Global counts and the appearance function cannot determine this first-collision timing; the theorem gives a natural complete classification rather than an arbitrary finite slice, parameter renaming, or small numerical gain.
